newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Origin sees strong 97 rise in ops income.
newsitem.headline: Origin sees strong 97 rise in ops income.

text.p: Information technology services provider Origin said on Wednesday it expected a strong increase in income from operations in 1997, despite further merger-related costs.

The company earlier announced a 1996 net loss of 108.2 million guilders, against a previous 23.0 million guilders profit, hit by the costs arising from the merger of BSO/Origin into Philips Communications and Processing. Philips owns 82 percent of Origin.
Origin reported a loss of 98 million guilders from operations for 1996, compared to a profit of 52 million in 1995. Sales rose to 2.43 billion from 1.93 billion.
"Against a background of strong sales growth, the results reflect a net loss due in part to costs associated with the merger," the company said in a statement.
"We have made significant progress in bringing together two very different but complementary organisations," Origin chief executive Tom Butler said in the statement.
The company said it incurred 120 million guilders of extraordinary costs in 1996 related to the merger and a 27.6 million guilder charge to apply new accounting principles.
Butler said the 1997 goal was to maintain growth at above the industry average and manage the business aggressively to contain costs and assure improved profitability.
